newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SAYS MERITS BEING EU MEMBER BY 2000.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SAYS MERITS BEING EU MEMBER BY 2000.

text.p: Hungary said on Wednesday that as one of the best placed applicants of the six recommended by the European Commission for early EU accession talks, its acceptance for membership could be ratified separately by 2000.

"These accession talks in themselves provide a method of differentiation...so there is also the possibility that the ratification process for one country might take place more easily and earlier than with others," Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs told a news conference.

The European Commission on Wednesday officially published a report recommending that Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Estonia and Slovenia should be invited to begin EU membership talks along with Cyprus next year.

Accession talks with prospective new members are expected to begin early in 1998 and to last two years before the ratification process begins, although EU External Relations Commissioner Hans Van der Broek said the negotiations could take longer in some cases.
"Each negotiation is separate and pursues its own course at a level which is deternined by the complexity of the issues to be resolved." he told the European Parliament on Wednesday.
EU officials have said that after the accession talks are completed, getting EU enlargement past the parliaments of the 15 member countries and applicant states could take until 2002.
However, Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn said earlier on Wednesday that Hungary should become a full EU member by 2000.

"I find it a well-founded hope that the 15 member countries will support Hungary's application and by 2000 Hungary will become a member of the European Union," Horn told a confernece of Hungarian ambassadors.
Kovacs said that as Hungary's case is strong, a separate ratification could happen quickly.
"Completing accession talks early in 2000...does not exclude the possibility that the ratification process might be concluded at the end of the year 2000," he said.

One of the bright stars in the eyes of the Commission, Hungary is seen as having successfully transposed the EU's laws in preparation for membership. It is judged well-placed to match up to competition in the medium term if it continues its efforts.

Kovacs said Hungary was satisfied with the European Commission's report and acknowledged areas in which improvements have still to be made, including aspects of the legal system, the rights of the Roma population and environmental protection.
"It would be irresponsible to say that accession talks can be finished very easily but to say the opposite would also be irresponsible," Kovacs said.
